# Results — Study 336 (Inverse-Cramer) on a curated real-call table

*Generated by re-running [`inverse_cramer`](../inverse_cramer/) over the **hardcoded curated
call table** ([`data.CALLS`](../inverse_cramer/data.py)) against real total-return daily
tapes (Yahoo via [`quantlab.data`](../../../quantlab/data.py), `mode='total_return'`). The
"fade" trades the **opposite** of each stated on-air direction, entered one session after the
call (one shift) and held a fixed forward window; it is pinned against a **random-direction
control** on the same calls, re-run with an extra execution day, swept for cost, and checked
against a deterministic synthetic control. As-of **2026-06-20**; match the per-ledger
fingerprint to confirm you hold the same tape.*

> **Read the sample warning first.** The 22-row call table is **curated for memorability** —
> it is the kind of "his worst calls" list a meme account assembles, i.e. a sample selected
> *on the outcome*. Every real number below inherits that bias. The synthetic control section
> shows how a coin-flip pundit produces a significant-looking fade once you publish only his
> worst calls. Nothing here certifies a real, tradable effect.

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Call table | 22 hardcoded on-air calls (2008–2022), curated |
| Tapes covered | 20 / 22 (BSC, SQ delisted under symbol → dropped) |
| Tape mode | total_return |
| Window | 2007-01-03 → 2026-06-18 |
| As-of | 2026-06-20 |
| Ledger fingerprint (fwd=21) | `a77316a2e802` |
| Ledger fingerprint (fwd=63) | `e31f20d44014` |

The two delisted symbols (BSC, FB→META rename, SQ→XYZ rename) being silently dropped is itself
part of the survivorship caveat: the most spectacular call (Bear Stearns "it's fine!") cannot
even be measured because the company ceased to exist — exactly the kind of call the meme leans
on but a price tape cannot honour.

## The headline — fade the curated calls, gross, fwd = 21 sessions

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/call) | skew | HAC *t* | boot 95% CI (bps) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| **Fade (−direction)** | 20 | **65.0%** | **+420.2** | −0.64 | **+1.47** | [−114, +937] |
| Random-direction control | 20 | 45.0% | +24.8 | — | — | — |

- The fade **looks** good — +420 bps/call, a 65% hit-rate, beating the coin by ~+395 bps.
- But at the meme's natural one-month horizon the HAC *t* is **+1.47 — below the inference
  bar (|t| ≥ 2)** — and the block-bootstrap CI on the mean **straddles zero** ([−114, +937]).
- With only 20 hand-picked calls there is simply not enough sample to certify anything, and
  the sample is selected to flatter the fade in the first place.

## Horizon sensitivity — the only "significant" result is the snoopable one

| Forward window | n | win-rate | mean (bps/call) | HAC *t* | boot 95% CI |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|---|
| 21 sessions (≈1 month, the meme horizon) | 20 | 65.0% | +420.2 | **+1.47** | [−114, +937] |
| 63 sessions (≈1 quarter) | 20 | 70.0% | +1220.4 | **+3.14** | [+327, +2049] |

The fade clears *t* = 2 only at the longer, **post-hoc-chosen** horizon — and on a sample
already curated against the pundit. Reaching for the horizon at which a selected sample turns
significant is exactly the data-snooping the inference bar forbids. We report the pre-declared
21-day horizon as the headline; the 63-day number is a sensitivity check, not a certificate.

## Look-ahead check — one extra execution day

| Entry lag | n | mean (bps/call) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| +1 session (canonical) | 20 | +420.2 | +1.47 |
| +2 sessions (conservative) | 20 | +537.0 | +2.26 |

The result is not a same-day-fill artefact, but it is *unstable* to a one-day shift (a 28%
swing in the mean from a single bar) — the fingerprint of a tiny, noisy sample, not a robust
edge.

## Could you trade it? — the cost sweep (fwd = 21, net)

| one-way cost (× 2 legs) | net mean (bps/call) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +420.2 | +1.47 |
| 5 bps | +410.2 | +1.44 |
| 10 bps | +400.2 | +1.40 |
| 20 bps | +380.2 | +1.33 |

Costs are *not* what kills this — the per-call moves are large. What kills it is that the
strategy is **unrunnable as stated**: the call list only exists in hindsight. You cannot trade
a curated table of past on-air moments; by the time a list of "his worst calls" exists, the
moves have already happened. A live "fade every Cramer call" rule would have to take *all* his
calls (hundreds a week), not the 20 that a meme remembers.

## Synthetic control — the harness, the null, and the curation trap

A deterministic synthetic universe of price paths plus pundit calls. One knob plants a
**genuine anti-signal** (the pundit is systematically wrong); a second plants **selection
bias** (the pundit is a coin, but the published list is curated to his worst calls). Seed 336,
n = 200 calls, fwd = 21.

| Synthetic tape | win-rate | mean (bps/call) | HAC *t* | reading |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| Null — coin pundit, no curation | 47.5% | −35.7 | **−0.54** | fade is a coin (correct) |
| Planted anti-signal (`anti_alpha=0.6`) | 79.5% | +449.8 | **+7.85** | engine detects a real anti-signal |
| **Selection bias only (`selection_bias=0.6`)** | **70.5%** | **+250.4** | **+4.14** | **a coin pundit looks fade-able once curated** |

The third row is the whole study in one line: a pundit with **zero predictive content**
produces a fade that clears *t* = 4 — purely because the call list was filtered to his worst
moments after the fact. The real curated table is the same machine, with a smaller n.

The positive control confirms the harness is faithful: the fade's edge over a coin rises
monotonically with the planted anti-signal and is ≈ 0 at the null.

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** On the meme's own one-month horizon the curated fade is **+420 bps/call
  at HAC *t* = +1.47**, below the |t| ≥ 2 bar, with a bootstrap CI straddling zero. It clears
  the bar only at a snooped longer horizon, on a sample selected to flatter it. The meme and a
  short-lived ETF (SJIM) assert a real anti-edge; this tape cannot certify it.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The strategy as stated is unrunnable: the call list exists only in
  hindsight. A live, *all-calls* version is the actual test, and the curated headline is not
  evidence for it. Costs are not the binding constraint — the absence of a tradable, forward
  rule is.
- **Selection bias? — NOT SUPPORTED (as an edge).** The synthetic control shows a coin-flip
  pundit manufactures a *t* = +4 fade once you publish only his worst calls. The curated
  table's apparent edge is consistent with pure curation. The "inverse the loudest pundit"
  edge is **not supported** once the selection is accounted for.
